concepts.name: Classification of Landslides by Movement Type
key_dimensions: Distinction between falls, flows, slides, spreads, and topples (Varnes Classification)
Debris flow vs. mudflow vs. earthflow — material composition differences
Rotational vs. translational slides — geometry and trigger conditions
UPSC trap: rockfall ≠ landslide in strictest sense, yet both covered under mass wasting

concepts.name: Geological Triggers: Role of Rock Type and Lithology
key_dimensions: Weak rocks (shales, clays, weathered granite) vs. competent rocks in slope stability
Presence of clay minerals (montmorillonite) reducing shear strength
Jointing, faulting, and foliation planes as failure surfaces
UPSC trap: Himalayan geology (young, tectonically active, friable) vs. stable Peninsular rock — why vulnerability differs

concepts.name: Role of Rainfall and Hydrology in Triggering Landslides
key_dimensions: Antecedent rainfall vs. intense short-duration rainfall — different pore pressure mechanisms
Threshold rainfall concept: intensity-duration-frequency relationships
Seepage, groundwater rise, and reduction of effective stress (Terzaghi's principle in context)
UPSC trap: cloud bursts in Western Ghats and Himalayas triggering flash floods AND landslides simultaneously

concepts.name: Seismic Activity as a Landslide Trigger
key_dimensions: Earthquake-induced landslides vs. rainfall-induced — speed, volume, and run-out distance differences
Liquefaction of saturated slopes during seismic shaking
Co-seismic vs. post-seismic landslides (delayed failure)
UPSC trap: Seismic Zone V overlap with landslide-prone zones — NE India, Uttarakhand, J&K

concepts.name: Anthropogenic Causes of Landslides
key_dimensions: Slope cutting for roads, railways, and construction — undercutting natural support
Deforestation reducing root cohesion and increasing surface runoff
Overloading slopes with construction and waste dumping
UPSC trap: Mining (overburden removal, blasting vibrations) as a distinct anthropogenic cause — Joshimath subsidence linkage

concepts.name: Deforestation and Vegetation Cover as a Risk Multiplier
key_dimensions: Root reinforcement mechanism — how tree roots increase shear strength of soil
Evapotranspiration reducing soil moisture saturation
Jhum cultivation (shifting agriculture) in NE India degrading hill slopes
UPSC trap: Afforestation alone is insufficient if geology is unfavorable — nuanced answer angle

concepts.name: Himalayan Region as a Primary Landslide Hotspot
key_dimensions: Young fold mountains — unconsolidated, tectonically stressed rock
High relief, steep gradients, and deeply incised river valleys
Monsoon intensification + glacial melt as dual hydrological triggers
UPSC trap: Distinguish Western Himalaya (J&K, Himachal, Uttarakhand) vs. Eastern Himalaya (Sikkim, Arunachal) vulnerability patterns

concepts.name: Western Ghats as a Secondary Landslide Vulnerable Zone
key_dimensions: Laterite soil over hard rock — susceptibility to slippage along interface
High intensity monsoon rainfall (Kerala, coastal Karnataka, Goa)
Plantation agriculture and encroachment on steep slopes
UPSC trap: Western Ghats landslides are more soil/debris flows, unlike rock falls in Himalayas — different hazard profile

concepts.name: North-East India: Unique Vulnerability Profile
key_dimensions: Highest seismicity in India (Seismic Zone V) combined with high rainfall
Fragile geology of Naga Hills, Manipur Hills, Mizoram ranges
Jhum cultivation degrading slope stability across tribal hilly areas
UPSC trap: NE India has both seismic AND hydro-meteorological triggers acting simultaneously — compound risk

concepts.name: National Landslide Susceptibility Mapping
key_dimensions: GSI (Geological Survey of India) as the nodal agency for landslide hazard zonation
Parameters used: slope angle, lithology, land use, drainage, rainfall, seismicity
Four hazard zones: Very High, High, Moderate, Low — and their spatial distribution
UPSC trap: Hazard map ≠ Risk map (risk incorporates exposure and vulnerability of population)

concepts.name: Landslide Dam and Outburst Floods (LDOF)
key_dimensions: Mechanism: landslide debris blocking river valley creating temporary reservoir
Catastrophic failure releasing flash floods downstream (e.g., Uttarakhand 2021 Chamoli, Rishi Ganga)
Distinction from Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) — often confused in UPSC questions
UPSC trap: Landslide dams are natural but GLOFs can also trigger landslides — cascading multi-hazard chain

concepts.name: Early Warning Systems for Landslides in India
key_dimensions: IMD rainfall threshold-based early warnings for landslide-prone districts
ISRO's Bhuvan portal and remote sensing for near-real-time landslide monitoring
Community-based early warning systems in pilot areas (Munnar, Darjeeling)
UPSC trap: India lacks a dedicated national landslide early warning network unlike Japan/Italy — governance gap angle

concepts.name: Sendai Framework and Landslide Disaster Risk Reduction
key_dimensions: Sendai Framework 2015–2030: four priorities and how landslide risk fits within
Priority 1 (Understanding Risk) — landslide hazard mapping as a tool
India's alignment: National Disaster Management Plan (NDMP) and landslide-specific guidelines
UPSC trap: Sendai is a non-binding framework — voluntary targets, not legally enforceable unlike Paris Agreement

concepts.name: NDMA Guidelines on Landslide Risk Management
key_dimensions: NDMA 2009 guidelines: prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response, recovery components
Recommendations on slope stabilization, drainage management, and land-use regulation
Role of State Disaster Management Authorities (SDMAs) in implementation
UPSC trap: NDMA guidelines are advisory, not mandatory — weak enforcement is a key criticism

concepts.name: Slope Stabilization and Engineering Mitigation Measures
key_dimensions: Structural measures: retaining walls, rock bolting, soil nailing, gabion structures
Drainage interventions: surface drains, sub-surface drains reducing pore water pressure
Bio-engineering: vetiver grass, bamboo, and native species for shallow slide prevention
UPSC trap: Engineering solutions are expensive and context-specific — not universally applicable; bio-engineering more sustainable for developing nations

concepts.name: Land-Use Planning and Regulation in Landslide Zones
key_dimensions: Restriction of construction in Very High Hazard Zones — policy vs. ground reality gap
Town and Country Planning Acts of states vs. national building codes applicability
Eco-Sensitive Zone (ESZ) notifications around Western Ghats and landslide prevention linkage
UPSC trap: ESZ boundaries are contested; Western Ghats Ecology Expert Panel (Gadgil vs. Kasturirangan) — conflicting recommendations on development restriction

concepts.name: Climate Change and Increasing Landslide Frequency
key_dimensions: Changing precipitation patterns: increased intensity of extreme rainfall events (IPCC AR6 findings)
Glacial retreat destabilizing valley slopes in high-altitude Himalayas
Permafrost thaw in higher Himalayas reducing slope cohesion
UPSC trap: Climate change is an indirect driver amplifying existing vulnerabilities, not a direct cause — important nuance for mains answers

concepts.name: Joshimath Land Subsidence: A Case Study in Anthropogenic Landslide Risk
key_dimensions: Geological setting: Joshimath sits on ancient landslide deposit — inherently unstable
Anthropogenic triggers: NTPC tunneling, Char Dham highway widening, unregulated construction
Distinction between subsidence and landslide — yet both under 'mass wasting' umbrella
UPSC trap: Joshimath is not just a development failure but also a failure of geological risk assessment before urbanization — governance + science angle

concepts.name: Role of GSI, ISRO, and NRSC in Landslide Monitoring
key_dimensions: GSI: primary geological survey and hazard zonation; maintains National Landslide Inventory
NRSC/ISRO: satellite-based landslide mapping using SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) and optical data
Overlap and coordination gaps between GSI, NRSC, IMD, and NDMA in integrated landslide management
UPSC trap: Multiple agencies with overlapping mandates — institutional fragmentation as a governance challenge, unlike single-window flood management under CWC

concepts.name: Socioeconomic Vulnerability and Landslide Risk
key_dimensions: Poor and marginalized communities occupying steep, unstable slopes due to land scarcity
Inadequate infrastructure (roads, drainage) in hilly tribal areas increasing exposure
Post-disaster recovery challenges: inaccessibility, supply chain disruptions in mountain regions
UPSC trap: Landslide risk is not purely physical — social vulnerability (caste, poverty, gender) determines who bears the greatest impact; links to Disaster Risk Governance and SDG 11
